# Project onboarding

Build useful story memory for revision: what is written, what is planned, which sources support it, and what a proposed change affects. This is operating guidance. Dedicated new-project intake and full-manuscript scale remain subject to the implementation plan's runtime checks.

## Reuse established story memory — John, 11 September 2026

After onboarding, begin routine writing sessions from the existing ledger, dossiers and structural maps. Read new or changed material; consult original passages only to resolve a specific evidence need or ambiguity. Exclude history by default unless particular material is deliberately restored. Do not reread the full core manuscript or historical collection at each session. Update affected claims and views through the existing incremental path while preserving source qualifications and prior author choices.

Required runtime evidence: default commit with no changed source makes zero extraction calls; one new or edited registered passage extracts only its changed scene or scenes, without recapturing unchanged or excluded historical material. These are verification obligations, not a claim that this guidance establishes a runtime pass.

## Choose the working sources

For a project with older recordings, set `chekhov/config.json` `ledger_sources` to the explicitly reviewed current source directories. This is the initial selection; the engine also retains exact new writing paths in `chekhov/commit.json` `source_files` after successful scoped capture. The union remains visible through acceptance. Invalid, missing, overlapping or escaping selections refuse; omitting `ledger_sources` retains the legacy recursive walk. Never use omission as a shortcut to activate old history. Narrowing the directories does not remove already registered writing files: reconcile those deliberately. Relocation alone does not activate sources or accept their claims. See [First writing session](first-writing-session.md) for the author workflow and source relocation contract.

Resolve the writing project's own root before choosing output paths. Author-facing deliverables, book views, recorded project data and rendered copies belong within that project, alongside its working materials; Skill Foundry is the skill's development home, not the destination for a writing project's documents. Respect the project's existing organization. For BrightHeart, current book deliverables live under `Rework 2026/Chekhov/Book N/`, with shared supporting records alongside them. A worker's temporary output directory is staging: relocate its completed files, verify them, and publish the project-local paths before delivery. Historical skill-run evidence may remain in the skill journal. Keep isolated candidate recordings distinct from an existing live managed ledger; relocation alone does not merge, activate or accept records.

Start with the working manuscript identified by the author or current project records. Compare content and version evidence when copies disagree; a newer timestamp alone does not establish authority. Preserve older versions as history and exclude them from default ingestion unless particular passages were deliberately restored. Resolve embedded chapter or line references against current text, searching distinctive phrases or passage content across selected book packets before declaring cited material missing. Check the intended scene's complete current boundaries; an old cited range may stop midway through it.

Record selected paths, hashes, roles and selection reasons through the existing project configuration and manifest. Keep current manuscript, current outline, Bible guidance, series possibilities and selected additional writing distinct. A fallible Bible is evidence to reconcile, not permission to overwrite the story or declare author-approved canon. Preserve the link from extracted text to its original document.

## Capture connected meaning

During initial onboarding of an established novel or series, first orient to the whole story using the manuscript and current planning guidance. Assemble coherent book-scale collections of relevant full passages, intended placement, additional writing and gaps, with shared series context. A substantial Bible is useful guidance; disagreement may indicate a planned revision rather than an erroneous Bible. Read a book's material together where practical, keeping shared or uncertain placements explicit. Choose divisions from source size and output needs; do not default to one model call per heading. Save useful work during the reading session instead of requiring one oversized final structured response.

Create book-level ledger views and a master view of the same claims, using shared identities and source links. Summaries do not replace the detailed ledger or original passages. Review allocation and omissions against sources, then resolve relationships across books. Less-developed future books retain their alternatives and open questions instead of acquiring invented certainty. A short story or seed idea need not use this book-level organization.

Before delivery, reconcile each reader's packet-only gaps against the other completed readings. Update the current book views and questions when the shared sources resolve a gap; preserve the original reading limits in provenance instead of asking the author to locate or rewrite material already found.

Capture setting, supported causal connections, what changes and stays the same in identity, role and knowledge, structural placement, and emotional consequences. Distinguish narration, character claims, unreliable cover stories, revelations, plans and author decisions. Preserve chronology, attribution and uncertainty. A character's statement is not automatically an unconditional world fact.

An exact-reference approach can let the model name a contiguous source passage while code supplies the quotation and provenance. Include all intervening text when a claim spans paragraphs; never stitch distant fragments into an apparent quotation. Preserve the original model response and the explicit projection into candidate tuples. Reject ambiguous or missing references through the existing validation path. Exact quotation binding and semantic entailment are separate checks: the whole claim and its qualifications must follow from the passage.

The existing writer binds each quotation within one detected heading. When evidence crosses headings, preserve separately anchored claims and their explicit relationship within the same coherent reading; this does not require additional model calls. Keep an original-to-corrected mapping for any narrowed or split records and independently check that the connection and qualifications survive storage.

Before importing, verify that every frozen source copy is actually discoverable by `projectDocuments` as the intended prose class. The `_source.md` suffix protects author-owned content but does not itself register an arbitrary filename for reading. Preserve original filenames and coordinates in provenance; record any copy-path mapping explicitly. Treat a successful commit with fewer candidates than expected as a failed import, preserve partial progress, and recover only the missing source records. Verify all prior records unchanged and every proposed record present after rebuilding. Bold headings count as boundaries in the current reader. (Formal0032: actual Book 4 discovery failure and recovery.)

## Read themes and structure at every meaningful level

Read both dimensions for each book, story or collection, its meaningful subsections, intermediate groups such as trilogies, and the whole work or series. Choose units with a narrative or organizing purpose; do not manufacture a separate analysis for every paragraph. A collection may preserve independent stories while using thematic progression, contrast or sequence to govern their selection and order.

For each theme, state the human question or position being explored. Identify the character choices, scenes and motifs that embody, test or complicate it, and the resolution or remaining wound. Distinguish source-backed interpretation from explicit author intention and a new idea; cite the supporting material or recorded author choice. Read trauma and healing allegories as literary meaning, without turning them into medical doctrine or claims about how people must recover.

**Theme clarity and review.** Use a graspable sentence, not a list of abstract topics. Test it against two or three decisive choices and consequences, including complications; distinguish written evidence from proposed material and identify a useful revision implication. Put sufficient depth beneath the short statement; do not force a moral, resolve intentional ambiguity or remove nuance.

Label unapproved meaning a **proposed working theme**. At normal feedback, present one theme at a time: sentence, concrete reason and recommendation. Record actual approval's exact meaning, scope and date through existing records; approval remains revisable and does not automatically lock canon. Reuse established author themes: wording-only clarification does not reopen meaning. Review material reinterpretation before promotion; draft work may continue provisionally.

Use a lightweight internal check against known material, without requiring a model panel per theme or permission for every scene. Apply the existing canonical Elegance rules without duplicating them here.

For each governing structure, name the selected framework and map actual or proposed events to its functions, showing how those functions govern organization. Mark what is written, planned or provisional, with gaps and viable options. Preserve the author's selected kishōtenketsu where applicable: identify what Ki establishes, how Shō develops it, what Ten recontextualizes and how Ketsu brings the resulting understanding together. Ten changes the understanding of preceding material; an arbitrary twist alone does not demonstrate that function. Four functions do not require four books, equal lengths or an absence of conflict. Other forms remain available. If the author has not selected a structure, propose a fitting provisional form and let the seed idea develop without treating that proposal as canon or requiring a choice before useful work can continue.

Carry the theme reading and structural map into the existing dossier and ledger readouts, and revisit the affected subsection, book, group and series when proposing revisions. Author feedback takes precedence; interpretations and suggestions retain candidate status until the author's actual choices support acceptance through the existing path. This is operating guidance for reading and editorial work, not a claim that automated theme extraction or structural validation is implemented.

Before calling the reading or revision review complete, inspect the actual deliverables for both dimensions at every applicable level. Check that themes have concrete evidence and structural labels have event mappings with organizational consequences. Repair omissions; where evidence or an author choice is still open, state the gap and provisional options explicitly rather than hiding the missing analysis behind a framework name.

## Prove usefulness before scaling

For a coherent reading that saves proposed records in durable files, use `lib/onboarding.mjs` to project the recorded claims into the existing commit replay format. Supply the operator's frozen source excerpts and hashes, actual reading receipt/prompt hash, and proposed original line references. The projector derives exact quotes, preserves source roles and proposed unit placement, and rejects invalid references or author-approval fields. `requestCommit` remains the only source-candidate writer; use an explicit scope for manuscript paths, then rebuild and inspect the existing index. Heading rows are reference bindings for replay, not separate model requests. Recordings and readable dossier/book/master files support one ledger; they do not become competing canon stores. This integration's current real-use evidence belongs in the active formal cycle, not inferred from a helper test.

Keep the initial-reading unit separate from incremental updates. Subsequent passage changes use ordinary scoped commit unless an observed failure requires another formal refinement. Product acceptance means the author finds the reviewed dossier useful and understands its open questions; it does not bulk-lock the extracted claims. Use the existing bounded acceptance path only for the author's actual choices.

Carry the author's feedback on an accepted example into the next agreed batch; a named next batch is already authorized. Use the agreed feedback point to pause dependent expansion. For a series, keep source-qualified cross-book links and questions current during each batch, then assemble the final series summary and master view after the agreed constituent-book coverage and feedback.

Present each book through its own readable guide and feedback step unless the author requests a combined review. Preparing several books concurrently does not require the author to review them together. Keep connections in the shared ledger, carry each book's feedback forward, and make the current book and the next queued book clear.

Use each companion document's actual filename as its visible guide-link label, including the extension matching the destination—for example, `BOOK6-DOSSIER.html` or `BOOK6-DOSSIER.md`. Keep "Book N" naming consistent. Preserve existing prose when repairing delivery; change only the affected links and requested labels. Project documents use ordinary relative file links, resolved from the document's own folder; never embed Anchor `/artifact/<id>` routes in their Markdown or local HTML. Rendered copies stay beside their Markdown sources, using the same descriptive basename and links to sibling rendered files. Resolve source citations back to the project's originals or clearly identified local source views. Before delivery, open the actual project-local results file in the intended reader, click every primary companion link without modifying the page or its link behavior, and exercise cross-document and source-line navigation. Check remaining destinations, anchors and project containment; distinguish those checks from actual browser clicks. Name the tested viewer and any unverified client boundary. A web-only test does not verify local file opening, and local file opening does not establish a web reader's behavior.

An operational timeout is not a quality deadline. Preserve durable outputs when a call is interrupted. The projector permits explicitly unreviewed, source-bound timeout output only with its actual failed receipt and saved-output digests; the operator verifies those bytes. Such candidates retain `origin_execution_status: interrupted` through storage. A separate completion call attests only its declared work and must never relabel the original execution successful. Full original-source meaning and omission review remains required before treating the product as ready. Use supported continuation where available; no blind full reread, fabricated success receipt or shared-driver patch.

Source-supported narrative links can explain consequences beyond the current deterministic graph. Preserve them as qualified analysis with original citations; the graph still derives only its documented edges. A store/rebuild check must prove those claims and citations survive, and an example revision must distinguish source-based reasoning from actual computed ripple results.

For a large existing project, use the first substantial book dossier and ledger in shared story context to prove the method. For smaller projects, use a coherent representative unit. Declare critical relationships and source spans before synthesis, keeping expected answers out of the authoring prompt. Preserve actual outputs, source roles, candidate status, omissions and measured time. Use existing candidate, replay, commit and index paths; no second ledger or candidate store. Ledger usefulness need not wait for unfinished writing-interface features.

Check actual stored meanings, not only quotation validity or record counts. Every critical fact must survive; a named omission is still a failure. Check the expectations against the source too. If an expectation proves unsupported, preserve the original and record a separate correction with its evidence; never invent a story connection or claim the original test passed. Qualify interpretations that go beyond explicit source statements.

Size the combined review packet before launching a model. Preserve complete new deliverables and their supporting passages and records; remove duplicated material before narrowing evidence. When earlier work has already been reviewed, identify that boundary and include its complete relevant evidence wherever the new synthesis relies on it. Do not imply a fresh exhaustive review of excluded material. Keep the actual review verdict after bounded corrections rather than relabeling it as a new pass.

Demonstrate one clearly hypothetical revision or edit using actual cited evidence. Explain affected passages, structural consequences, an alternative where useful, and unresolved questions. Keep suggested prose visibly unaccepted and avoid claiming voice matching without its validation.

Refine demonstrated misses in a bounded focused recovery. If material gaps remain, record their disposition and defer scaling; avoid repeated generic approval rounds. A successful fact-only sample does not prove thread or form extraction, whole-manuscript coverage, full-scale cost, or ordinary idea-response latency. Preserve existing capture contracts and checkpoints when integrating a new recorded mode.

## Begin writing and learning

Group consequential conflicts or proposed edits by the underlying decision, and order prerequisites before dependent questions. Present one necessary choice at a time with plain context, relevant passages, consequences and a recommendation. Keep nonblocking uncertainty visible while continuing other work. Use the existing acceptance and decision paths; update affected book views and the master from the same decision. Incorporate later writing and repeat relevant checks as the story changes; candidate facts remain provisional until accepted.

Use one shared series question for a decision affecting several books, with links from the book views and their specific consequences retained. Current guidance supplies the working recommendation; keep material alternatives that change agency or causal structure visible without turning every older variant into another mandatory question.

With only a vague idea, begin with a provisional seed brief and explicit unknowns. A Bible is not a prerequisite. Offer short voice or structure alternatives when they help the next choice; keep examples exploratory. Focused, cited research can answer a specific story question without implying an automated research feature. Grow the brief into draft material, then apply the same source, capture and revision checks.
